sections.h2: What should a Woodford County home seller know about the county?
sections.html:
Prairie, bluffs and cropland define Woodford County, which belongs to the Peoria metro area. Total area is 543 square miles, with 528 on land. Tazewell and McLean counties gave up territory to form it in February 1841, and an 1894 vote moved the courthouse from Metamora to Eureka, where it remains.

A population of 38,467 lived in 14,616 households at the 2020 census. Rural areas hold about 70% of residents, and owners live in 82.9% of occupied homes. Three places are legally cities: Eureka, El Paso and Minonk. Villages include Metamora, Roanoke, Germantown Hills, Goodfield, Washburn, Secor, Benson, Congerville, Panola, Kappa and Spring Bay. Eureka College, the school Ronald Reagan attended, sits in the seat.

Seventeen townships make up the county, running alphabetically from Cazenovia and Clayton to Spring Bay and Worth. Districts serving it include Eureka CUD 140, El Paso-Gridley 11, Fieldcrest 6, Roanoke-Benson 60, Lowpoint-Washburn 21, Olympia 16 and Deer Creek-Mackinaw 701. Eureka's January lows average 13 degrees and its July highs 86. The county is run by a 15-member elected board drawn from three districts, and the board levies the county's own share of taxes. Adjoining counties are Marshall, LaSalle, Livingston, McLean, Tazewell and Peoria.

sections.h2: Which Woodford County offices handle assessments and tax bills?
sections.html:
Three offices sit inside the courthouse at 115 N. Main Street in Eureka, so a single visit can cover assessment, appeal and payment questions.

Woodford County property tax offices (source: county website)
OfficeRoleLocation and phone
Supervisor of AssessmentsOwner records, values, exemptions, parcel splits; does not calculate or collect taxRoom 101; 309-467-3708
Board of ReviewHears assessment appeals; clerk work is done in the assessment officeRoom 101; open weekdays 9 a.m. to 4 p.m.
County Treasurer and CollectorMails bills, collects, distributes to taxing districtsRoom 105; 309-467-4621

The assessment office reports that it answers for more than 25,000 parcels. Its goal is an accurate, uniform value for each, with homes, businesses and factories assessed at 33 1/3% of market value. A township-by-township comparison of sale prices with assessed values yields the yearly equalization factor.

On the collection side, the Treasurer mails over 25,000 real estate bills, collects more than $83 million and distributes it among over 102 taxing districts. The Supervisor of Assessments does not calculate taxes, set rates or collect them, so disputes over a parcel's value belong in the assessment office. If your neighborhood's assessment looks out of line, the equalization factor for your township is a good question to ask when you call.

sections.h2: What is the Woodford County property tax calendar?
sections.html:
The Treasurer describes a pattern, not a fixed date. Mailing is usually in May, the first payment falls 30 days after that, and the second payment falls on the first Friday in September. One bill arrives with a payment coupon for each half.

Two other dates matter to sellers and buyers:

  • The yearly tax sale is held in late October.
  • Mobile home bills are mailed in March and are due 60 days after the mailing date.

Current and earlier bills can be looked up through the county's property tax search page, which helps a seller who has lost the paper copy. For the cost of a late payment or a redemption figure, call 309-467-4621, because those totals depend on the day you pay.

sections.h2: How does an appeal reach the Woodford County Board of Review?
sections.html:
A window of 30 days opens when the assessment office prints that year's assessment changes in local newspapers. Values on a bill already in hand cannot be appealed, since that bill reflects the prior year. Arguments about tax dollars fail too, as the Board has no authority over district budgets.

What the Board's guidelines and rules call for:

  • Owners of non-farm property complete PTAX-230 plus its addendum, and farm owners use PTAX-227 plus the farmland addendum.
  • Where buildings exist, state the land value and the improvement value separately.
  • Attach evidence for your view of fair cash value; an appraisal with supporting documentation qualifies.
  • Sign the appeal as owner and hand it to the Board's clerk in the assessment office.

The Board starts work by the first Monday in June, in Room 104 of the original courthouse building. Appellants get a mailed hearing time or a proposed action. Asking for a hearing on a proposed action takes a request within 10 days, and failing to show up for a noticed hearing can dismiss the appeal. A written decision is promised within 30 days of the hearing, and the final decision can go on to the Illinois Property Tax Appeal Board.

Separately, the Board may issue a Certificate of Error for the previous assessment year until 5:00 p.m. on the day ahead of the tax sale. Its rules count duplicate assessments, arithmetic slips, improvements destroyed before the assessment date and a missed homestead exemption as factual errors. Matters of judgment, including a building's quality grade, do not qualify.

sections.h2: Which Woodford County homestead exemptions can a seller or buyer claim?
sections.html:
Every real property exemption runs through the assessment office. Its forms page lists the applications below, and renewals must be requested from the office.

  • The owner-occupied exemption form.
  • PTAX-324, the senior homestead exemption application.
  • PTAX-323, for home improvements.
  • PTAX-343 and PTAX-343-R, covering disabled persons with the physician's statement and renewal.
  • PTAX-342 and PTAX-342-R, the disabled veteran forms.
  • PTAX-330, for solar.

Property owned by governments and religious institutions follows the non-homestead path, using form PTAX-300. The Board adds its recommendation and the Department of Revenue has the last word. Because amounts and income limits shift with state law, call 309-467-3708 for current figures before pricing a house around a reduction.

The office describes homestead exemptions as meant for taxpayers who own and live in the property, so a buyer moving in is the one to apply. The same office has forms for name and address changes, parcel splits and parcel consolidation.

sections.h2: What if a Woodford County bill goes unpaid?
sections.html:
Delinquent parcels are offered at the late-October tax sale, where a buyer pays the unpaid tax. Illinois law sets the penalty and interest that build up and the time an owner has to redeem. The Treasurer can tell you where a parcel stands, and the County Clerk can quote redemption.

The sale also sets the cutoff for Certificates of Error. A factual mistake, such as an exemption that was never applied, can be fixed by the Board until the afternoon before the sale, so check a bill early.

sections.h2: How is the Woodford County tax bill handled at closing?
sections.html:
Begin with the parcel's payment status, then settle the year in progress on the closing statement. Bills arrive a year in arrears, so the September installment can cover a year the seller owned the house even after a spring or summer closing.

Before signing, check three things:

  • The parcel record shows both halves of the latest bill as paid.
  • The closing agent has prorated the current year and listed the credit on the settlement statement.
  • A divided farm or acreage tract has its parcel split request finished so the buyer's bill carries the right number.

faqs.q: What day is the second half payable in Woodford County?
faqs.a: The first Friday in September. The first half is payable 30 days after the usual May mailing.

faqs.q: What is the filing window for a Woodford County assessment appeal?
faqs.a: Thirty days, counted from the date the assessment office publishes the year's changes in local newspapers. The values on a bill you already hold are not open to appeal.

faqs.q: Who works out the tax amount in Woodford County?
faqs.a: Not the Supervisor of Assessments, which handles values and exemptions only. The taxing districts' levies set the amount, and the Treasurer collects.

faqs.q: Is a Woodford County Board of Review ruling final?
faqs.a: No. The county's guidelines say the notice of final decision may be appealed to the Illinois Property Tax Appeal Board.

faqs.q: What month is the Woodford County tax sale?
faqs.a: Late October. Mobile home bills run on their own schedule: mailed in March, payable 60 days afterward.
